newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo stocks end higher for third straight day.
newsitem.headline: Colombo stocks end higher for third straight day.

text.p: Buying touched off by soaring plantation shares pushed Sri Lankan stocks to a higher close for the third consecutive day on Friday, but brokers warned of profit-taking in the short-term.
The all share index rose 3.94 points to 572.84, with gainers outnumbering decliners by 24 to 13.
"Some investors are using the current low price levels for long-term investment," said Sriyan Gurusinghe of Bartleet Mallory Stock Brokers.
The index, which was searching for direction, was buoyed by the optimism generated in plantation shares, brokers said.

"It was optimism in plantation shares that helped the index to break out of its groove. But there is selling waiting at around 575 to 580, which will cap the upward movement," said Gurusinghe. Tea prices are near-record levels currently.
Ceylon Oxygen rose 4.50 rupees to 52, Commercial Bank 4,75 to 96.75.

Turnover was 25.7 million rupees on 1.8 million shares, supported by foreign buying of 922,000 Asia Capital shares, which stayed unchanged at seven rupees, and 207,000 Ceylon Brewery which fell 50 cents to 31.50, brokers said.
